# Q2 / Q3 analysis: F3-A A25(a) authority_domain and A25(e) host/effective profile digest member isolation

Status: READ-ONLY static source analysis of frozen subject 739efe7d8f16a0cee1efc7dd3a978d5d4d85fe69 (unpacked tree /tmp/claude-0/work/src/cp-739efe7; paths below are relative to src/agent_control_plane/ unless stated).
Nothing was executed, no candidate test was run, no repo or guard was modified. Every route labelled "predicted" is UNVERIFIED BY EXECUTION: the first step of the fresh worker must be a feasibility probe that is recorded whatever it shows.
No claim of end-to-end isolation is made from component evidence anywhere below.

## 0. Summary of conclusions

1. scope.authority_domain (Q2): natural live-side isolation is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE. The member is a pure function of the manifest, and the manifest digest is itself a base-binding member that every execute must match. Any supported way of making the live domain differ changes bounded manifest_digest (and proposal_commitment) as well, and two upstream reason guards fire first for the un-rebuilt proposal. A route that DOES isolate the member is the GRAFT route (section 3.A, route R5): a genuine member minted by production code in a real d1 world is placed (unsigned-store write, documented limit, no guard disabled) into a genuine decision minted in a real d2 world; the only difference between persisted and live ECB members is then authority_domain, and every base field is equal. It isolates the comparison plus live derivation; it does not show a natural route.
2. host_profile_digest (Q3a): CONTRARY to the original A25(e) record, true end-to-end isolation through supported interfaces appears REACHABLE (predicted, unexecuted) on a class-age (F5) workflow, because compose_profile overwrites the host class age with the Registry-narrowed value, so a host edit that is fully masked yields the SAME effective profile, SAME catalogue_digest, SAME approval_commitment, SAME family digests, but a DIFFERENT host_profile_digest. The original attempt used the pin-export fixture (F4-only family + policy_binding), where effective profile == host profile (G5a: both digests == catalogue_digest), so no masking was possible there. The candidate's own doc (docs/effective-configuration-binding.md at 8616d5f, section 10 masked-host bullet) states exactly this: "any change to the host PROFILE (host_profile_digest is a member, so a host profile edit is refused even if the final profile is identical)".
3. effective_profile_digest (Q3b): STRUCTURALLY not isolable end-to-end. It is the same digest function over the same held object as persisted catalogue_digest (runtime_authority.py:475 vs registry_f5_class_age_governance.py:130-132/260, registry_governed_policy.py:482-486), and the approval_commitment is computed over the same profile. Any natural live change moves catalogue_digest (base binding) and, unless the approval is re-issued, trips runtime_authority_approval_mismatch first. Only component evidence, a binding-diff attribution (joint), and the persisted-side reseal already passed in A19 are available; a live-side graft is possible but needs a donor with a different effective profile and therefore differs in more members unless the freshness-extension construction in R-E4 is used.
4. Recommended deliverable for the fresh worker: 8 cases (section 6) built on the original harness-final library plus one new F5 class-age fixture builder.

## 3. Candidate routes: does each isolate, and why / why not

### 3.A scope.authority_domain
R1 Live-side rebuild with different manifest domain, original proposal and original resolver context (the original A25(a)). Does NOT isolate. manifest_digest_mismatch (:2619) and authority_domain_mismatch (:2297-2298) fire at step 3 and step 4 returns before the ECB is consulted.
R2 Live-side rebuild, fully consistent d2 world (manifest M2, Registry re-signed for d2, resolver context institution.authority_domain=d2, NEW proposal P2 with manifest_digest=commitment(M2)), executed against the d1 decision. Predicted: step 3 produces reasons [] (needs a feasibility probe: the synthetic resolver contexts must also be internally consistent for d2); step 6 emits [authorization_binding_changed] BUT overdetermined: the persisted base binding has manifest_digest(M1), proposal_commitment(P1) (bounded.py binding fields :264-291; :2577-2580 manifest_digest=proposal.manifest_digest) which differ from the live ones. Does NOT isolate the member; use only as the JOINT end-to-end refusal evidence, attributed by a binding-diff.
R3 Persisted-side edit of member.scope.authority_domain with resealed digest (the passing A19 execute row [scope.authority_domain], rows 520-798 and MEMBER_LEAVES 372-). Isolates the COMPARISON for that leaf (persisted-sensitivity) with live == original; cannot distinguish a constant live value (mutant M06 survived exactly for this reason, runs/A-mutants/RESULTS.md:8). Reuse, do not rely on it for live-side sensitivity.
R4 Direct component calls: ecb.scope_identity / build_members / mint / classify (pure; effective_configuration_binding.py:130-132,158-166,113-119,193-209) and the public read-only workflow.configuration_binding_status(decision) (lifecycle :252-261). Isolates the derivation or the comparison per call but as a COMPONENT; configuration_binding_status on a d2-world workflow with a genuine d1 decision object returns MISMATCH purely from member inequality (the decision need not be in the store; index None is irrelevant for BOUND/MISMATCH). This is real live-side derivation (the d2 workflow computes its own member) through a supported public method, but it is classification evidence, not a refusal.
R5 GRAFT (donor member): (i) mint decision D1 in world 1 (domain d1); (ii) in a separate store mint decision D2 in world 2 (domain d2, consistent resolver, own proposal P2, Registry re-signed); (iii) overwrite D2.binding.runtime_authority["effective_configuration"] in the store file with D1's member verbatim (a genuine, self-consistent member produced by production code; no reseal, no hand edit of any field); (iv) restart world 2; execute P2/D2. Predicted: persisted base binding == live base binding (identical world 2), persisted member vs live member differ only in scope.authority_domain (all other members identical provided both worlds use the same Registry values/scalars: family effective_policy_digest depends only on effective values, registry_f5_class_age_governance.py:180, so equal). Steps 0-5 raise nothing, step 6 emits exactly [authorization_binding_changed] with no attempt and no destination call. Unsigned-store writer capability is a documented limit (docs 'rollback/forge', harness case "forge"); no mandatory guard is disabled; effect_id does not cover runtime_authority so the "immutable persisted decision" check (bounded.py:1676) compares the store-reread object to itself. This is the only route found that DOES isolate through supported interfaces, and under the mutant M06 (constant domain) both members are equal so the execute SUCCEEDS, killing M06 end-to-end. Label route GRAFT, evidence class "isolated by store-level construction; not a natural-reachability claim".
R6 Subclass hook override (_gl_configuration_members, lifecycle :193-197 abstract hook; production subclasses at the four sites in section 1). Overriding it in a test subclass replaces the derivation under test; it can only show the comparison is live-sensitive, and it cannot kill derivation mutants (M06 changes scope_identity, which the override would bypass or reuse). Unsupported as isolating evidence for derivation; admissible only labelled PATCH-like. Not recommended.
R7 In-process patch of ecb.scope_identity or of lifecycle._gl_authority after construction: _gl_reverify :307-309 trips manifest_authority_changed only when the manifest changes; patching _gl_authority alone yields a member change with the manifest unchanged and would isolate, but it is a held-state mutation of a private attribute (PATCH, not supported; also not a mandatory-guard bypass). Mention only as PATCH parallel to A25(b)-(d); not recommended given R5.
Structural proof of non-isolability on natural routes: member value = authority[1] = manifest action authority_context.authority_domain (lifecycle :88,:174); binding.manifest_digest = proposal.manifest_digest (bounded.py:~2577) and must equal commitment(self.manifest) (bounded.py:2619); commitment covers the whole manifest including that authority_context. Hence member(authority_domain) is functionally dependent on a base-binding member, and the resolver must agree (bounded.py:2297-2298).

### 3.B host_profile_digest

Rebuild the same store with H2 identical to H1 except t1=61 (still > R). Then: derive_effective (registry_f5_class_age_governance.py:135-188) gives effective {T1:10} for both (min rule :172; widens-host :170 not hit); compose_profile (:117-127) overwrites the class age => effective profile identical => profile_digest(held) identical => catalogue_digest, approval_commitment (approval issued once against the effective profile, re-bound is unnecessary because it is identical), family effective_policy_digest (identity.effective_policy_digest(FAMILY, {FIELD: effective}) :180), f4/other scalars, observation all identical; held guards pass (:246-250); only host_profile_digest = profile_digest(self._f5_host) (:260) differs. Steps 0-5: no foreign reason; step 5 returns reasons [] and stamped binding != persisted by the ECB member only; step 6 => [authorization_binding_changed], PermissionError, one durable row, no attempt, destination untouched. Same via GovernedPolicyWorkflow with a class_age family but NOT with the pin fixture (policy_binding is refused for profile-bearing families: registry_governed_policy.py:333-336 policy_binding_unsupported). Must also keep freshness=None (or extension 0) so compose_profile's extension arithmetic (:123-126, room = min(registry-effective) = 0 for narrowed classes) cannot introduce an effective difference; with extension>0 it still masks (room 0) but keep it out of the minimum plan.
    Attribution proof (not oracle-by-candidate): in-test compute commitment(flow_H1.runtime_authority_profile.model_dump(mode="json")) == commitment(flow_H2....) and equal persisted/live catalogue_digest, and a binding-diff (section 5) whose only differing leaf is ...effective_configuration.members.host_profile_digest and the digest.
    Mutant that this separates: host_profile_digest := effective digest (or None). Under it H2 executes. Propose as scratch-copy mutant D06-M14 (PROPOSAL, scratch only, never the checkout).
R3 Persisted-side edit with reseal (A19 execute [host_profile_digest], PASS, reused): isolates the comparison, not live derivation.
R4 Direct component: workflow.effective_configuration_binding (policy only, :472-474) or the persisted member of a freshly minted decision; configuration_binding_status. Live-side derivation evidence for each digest (F5 fixture with host != effective).
R5 GRAFT: as in 3.A but donor = H1 member; world 2 = H2. With R2 available GRAFT is unnecessary for this member.
Documentation consistency: docs/effective-configuration-binding.md (8616d5f) masked-host bullet says a profile edit is refused even if the final profile is identical; R2 would confirm or contradict a candidate claim with a direct execution, which is exactly the independent test the doc lacks (the doc says the F4-scalar case 'has no dedicated test').

### 3.C effective_profile_digest
R1 Natural rebuild with a different effective profile (e.g. Registry R changed): moves catalogue_digest and approval_commitment too; the old approval does not match the new commitment => runtime_authority_approval_mismatch (runtime_authority.py:332-335) fires first (step 3e) and the ECB is not consulted. Re-issuing the approval for the new effective profile (bind_approval, a supported host duty: "approvals are issued against the final profile", registry_f5_class_age_governance.py:10-16) clears the reason; then current != persisted via catalogue_digest, approval_commitment, ECB effective_profile_digest and family effective_policy_digest TOGETHER. JOINT, not isolating.
R2 Hypothesis route (freshness extension): choose host age h and Registry values R1, R2 both >= h (so effective={T1:h} and family digest unchanged) with a freshness profile having max_age_extension_seconds E > R_i-h; compose_profile (:123-126) gives extension min(E, R_i-h) differing between R1 and R2, so effective profile differs while host profile and family digests are unchanged. This separates effective_profile_digest from OTHER ECB members, but it still moves catalogue_digest and approval_commitment (same digest/profile), so the end-to-end refusal is never member-isolated. Heavy (freshness/0.1 fixture). Optional only.
R3 Persisted-side reseal (A19 execute [effective_profile_digest], PASS): reuse.
R4 Component: member.effective_profile_digest == commitment(held.model_dump) == persisted catalogue_digest == (pin) host digest; on F5 fixture != host digest. Independent recomputation in the test.
R5 GRAFT: a donor from a world with different effective profile necessarily has a different catalogue_digest/approval; grafting its member into a world-2 decision does isolate (base binding equal to live world-2, member differs by effective_profile_digest plus whatever the donor world differs in, which with R2-hypothesis is only that digest). Possible but depends on R2's freshness fixture; otherwise the donor also differs in family digests (joint). Not recommended.
Structural statement: effective_profile_digest is redundant with catalogue_digest in the same persisted dict; a mutant that drops or constants the member is outcome-equivalent end-to-end for natural routes (killed only by component/graft evidence). 

## 4. Why the original verdict said UNREACHABLE-ISOLATED, and the corrected reading
* (a): correct for natural routes (reasons authority_domain_mismatch + manifest_digest_mismatch are the first guards); incomplete because the GRAFT route and the public read-only classifier route were not tried. M06 was killed in the readjudication by G5a content evidence (a constant-domain value differs from the independent expectation) which establishes derivation content, not live sensitivity.
* (e): correct for the pin fixture (host==effective). NOT correct as a general statement: for host_profile_digest the F5 masked-host construction (3.B R2) is a supported live-side route. For effective_profile_digest the statement stays correct (3.C).

## 5. Evidence decomposition (what each establishes and does NOT establish)

E-COMP (component equality; no refusal claim)
* Member content: persisted/live member scope.authority_domain == independent expectation from the manifest (G5a pattern) in two worlds d1, d2 with member diff == {scope.authority_domain}; host_profile_digest == independent commitment(host.model_dump); effective_profile_digest == independent commitment(held.model_dump) == persisted catalogue_digest, with host != effective on an F5 fixture; public read-only configuration_binding_status(D1) on a d2 workflow == "mismatch", (D2) == "bound" (candidate classifier is EVIDENCE ONLY; the oracle is the test's own member dict comparison).
* Establishes: the live derivation reads the right sources and distinguishes values; the equality used by classify is member-sensitive. Does NOT establish: that execute refuses, nor that any natural scenario reaches this comparison.

E-E2E (end-to-end refusal evidence)
* (a) natural: reasons == [authority_domain_mismatch, manifest_digest_mismatch] (R1) and joint [authorization_binding_changed] with the binding-diff (R2): establishes the decision is refused, with the first guard named; does NOT establish the member's contribution.
* (a) isolated by GRAFT (R5): single [authorization_binding_changed], base-binding diff empty, member diff {scope.authority_domain}: establishes the member alone produces the refusal in the real execute path with live derivation; does NOT establish natural reachability, and relies on the documented unsigned-store writer capability.
* (e-host) masked-host rebuild (3.B R2): if it runs as predicted this is TRUE end-to-end isolation for host_profile_digest; if the feasibility probe shows another guard fires, record the guard and fall back to GRAFT + component.
* (e-effective) joint only: [runtime_authority_approval_mismatch] without re-issue; [authorization_binding_changed] with a binding-diff that includes catalogue_digest/approval_commitment with re-issue.

E-REACH (reachability / guard-order proof)
* Static: the order table in section 2 with file:line; the dependency chain authority_domain <- manifest <- manifest_digest in binding (section 3.A proof); effective_profile_digest == catalogue_digest by construction (section 1). Mechanised check inside the test: for each end-to-end case compute the binding-diff between the persisted binding and the binding the live world mints for the same proposal (decide in a scratch store, or reconstruct from a genuine decide in the live world) and assert the set of differing leaves. A case may be called "isolated" only if that set is exactly {runtime_authority.effective_configuration.members.<m>, ...digest}; otherwise "joint" with the set recorded.
* Establishes: which guard is first and why a member cannot be alone on a route. Does NOT establish member sensitivity (that is E-COMP/GRAFT).

Evidence claims allowed in the verdict: (a) "refused (joint); member isolated only by GRAFT; natural isolation structurally impossible (proof in section 3.A)"; (e-host) "isolated end-to-end" only if the masked-host case passes with an empty complementary diff; (e-effective) "joint only; member-level sensitivity by component + persisted-reseal (A19)". Never "A25(a)/(e) PASS" from component evidence alone.
